subject: Dedicated capacity vs hyperscaler GPU offering - follow-up & next tests
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Sally Johnson <sally.johnson@acme.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@acme.ai>
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 15:10:00 +0000
Subject: Recap: Dedicated capacity vs hyperscaler GPU options (next steps)

Hi Sally / Tom,

Thanks again for the call today — appreciate the clarity on Acme's Q2 inference runway and the production SLOs for low-latency recommendations. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Summary of needs we captured
- Sustained throughput target: ~1.2M tokens/day (peak bursts to 2.5M tokens/day)
- P95 latency target: <250ms for 90% of requests
- Data controls: VPC + customer-managed KMS required
- Availability requirement: 99.9% monthly uptime SLA with planned maintenance windows

How Redwood maps to that (high level)
- Dedicated: reserved GPU pools with capacity guarantees, configurable autoscaling policy, and private VPC option (fits KMS requirement)
- Hyperscaler reserved instances (what you currently run in POC): cheaper upfront but less predictable during cross-service contention and less turnkey for inference-specific autoscaling/fallbacks

Proposed tests / next steps
1) Performance sanity test (this week): we run a 48-hour test on Redwood Dedicated with your 95th percentile load profile and the same model from your hyperscaler POC. We’ll produce latency and throughput heatmaps and a token cost comparison. (I attached a one-pager that outlines test scope.)
2) Failover & preemption scenario: demonstrate behavior under GPU contention — how Dedicated handles autoscaling and how hyperscaler reserved instances may be impacted.
3) Capex/opex comparison: we’ll share a 12-month TCO with reserved Dedicated pricing vs your hyperscaler baseline and show break-even points.

Attachments: Redwood_Dedicated_vs_Hyperscaler_OnePager.pdf (test scope) and MAP-Action-Plan.xlsx (mutual action plan draft)

Please confirm: 48-hour test start window — would Wednesday 2026-03-04 or Friday 2026-03-06 work for your engineering team to kick off? Also confirm the model name+quantization used in your POC so we spin up compatible variants.

Thanks,

Markus Klein

Thanks Markus — great recap.

We can do the 48-hour performance sanity test starting Friday 2026-03-06 at 09:00 PT. Confirmed model from POC is: "llama-70b-q4f16" (custom tokenizer). Our SRE will join the call for onboarding. For the preemption scenario, we’d like you to show behavior when a fraction (20-30%) of GPUs are taken offline to simulate cross-tenant contention — that mirrors what we see on our hyperscaler runs during big infra events.

A couple of clarifying Qs: 
- For Dedicated, do you guarantee no preemption of reserved capacity during our contracted window, or is there a reservation/burst model?
- For the pricing TCO, can you include an explicit line showing any enterprise support/observability add-ons (monthly) since we care about total landed cost?

Tom (cc) — can you share the POC telemetry dump and the exact inference config (batch size, concurrency, seq length distribution) so Markus’s team can reproduce it?

Sally
